title: Outlook: send local Word, Excel and PowerPoint files by email from the new Outlook for Windows
summary: The briefing's rollout windows, default state and mailbox-access command are supported by Microsoft's notice and documentation. Its statement about unpublished prerequisites should explicitly refer to requirements specific to sharing local Office files, rather than the documented requirements of the new Outlook itself.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to let users email a copy of a locally stored Word, Excel or PowerPoint file through the new Outlook for Windows while the file is open.
claims.quote: When working in an open Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file, users will now be able to send a copy of the locally stored file by email through the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The notice describes no new data access beyond users sending copies of local files.
claims.quote: Searched: Read MC1245222 in full for data-access changes. It describes sending locally stored files as email attachments, says existing Outlook/Exchange policies continue to apply, and identifies no compliance considerations; it states no additional data-access mechanism.

claims.claim: The roadmap item and notice describe no identity or sign-in change.
claims.quote: Searched: Read roadmap 557675 and supplied MC1245222 in full for identity and sign-in changes. Neither describes such a change; both describe user-initiated sharing of local Office files through new Outlook.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes users sending files they are working in, rather than autonomous action.
claims.quote: When working in an open Word, Excel, or PowerPoint file, users will now be able to send a copy of the locally stored file by email through the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents the general new Outlook feature sequence as Targeted Release for 30 days, then Standard Release (General Availability).
claims.quote: In new Outlook, new features become available first in Targeted Release for 30 days and then are rolled out to Standard Release (General Availability).

claims.claim: MC1245222 gives General Availability windows but no feature-specific Targeted Release dates.
claims.quote: Searched: Read MC1245222 in full for Targeted Release dates. Its rollout section lists only General Availability (Worldwide) and General Availability (GCC). Read manage-updates-new-outlook-windows, which gives a general sequence rather than dates for this feature.

claims.claim: The planned sharing feature requires the new Outlook for Windows.
claims.quote: users will now be able to send a copy of the locally stored file by email through the new Outlook for Windows.

claims.claim: Other prerequisites are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: new Outlook local files prerequisites. Read deployment-new-outlook and licensing-options: product requirements are published, but no additional prerequisite for this sharing feature was found.
claims.fix: Replace 'Other prerequisites are not yet published.' in Scope with 'Prerequisites specific to sending local Office files are not yet published.' The new Outlook's general deployment prerequisites are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365-apps/outlook/get-started/deployment-new-outlook.

claims.claim: No admin UI path is documented for the OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled mailbox-access setting.
claims.quote: Searched: OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled admin center. Read enable-disable-employee-access-new-outlook, control-install and policy-management: this setting is documented through PowerShell, not an admin UI.

claims.claim: Set-CASMailbox -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled $false disables new Outlook access to the specified mailbox through Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
Set-CASMailbox -Identity <MailboxIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled <$true | $false | $null>
This example disables Outlook for Windows for the specified user.

claims.claim: The existing mailbox-access control prevents use of new Outlook for that account, and therefore prevents using this feature through that account rather than switching off only this feature.
claims.quote: their account is disabled in Outlook for Windows and they can no longer use Outlook for Windows with that account. The user can delete the account from Outlook for Windows and then use Outlook for Windows with another account.

claims.claim: Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled $false makes the same access decision at mailbox-policy level.
claims.quote:
To enable or disable access to mailboxes in Outlook for Windows in Outlook on the web mailbox policies, use the following syntax:
Set-OwaMailboxPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdentity> -OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled <$true | $false | $null>

claims.claim: The mailbox-policy setting affects all current and future mailboxes that have that policy applied.
claims.quote: The value you specify in the Outlook on the web mailbox policy affects all current and future mailboxes that have the policy applied to them.

claims.claim: Microsoft directs administrators to the Outlook on the web mailbox policies entry in Feature permissions in Exchange Online for the permissions needed for this procedure.
claims.quote: To see what permissions you need, see the "Outlook on the web mailbox policies" entry in the Feature permissions in Exchange Online article.

claims.claim: The OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled cmdlets do not affect the availability of the Try the new Outlook toggle in classic Outlook.
claims.quote: The OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled parameter on the Set-CASMailbox or Set-OwaMailboxPolicy cmdlets doesn't affect the availability of the Try the new Outlook toggle in classic Outlook.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes True or blank for the mailbox's OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled property as access enabled.
claims.quote: The value True or blank for the OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled property means access is enabled.

claims.claim: OneWinNativeOutlookEnabled describes access permission, not actual usage.
claims.quote: The cmdlets determine whether users can open their work or school mailboxes in Outlook for Windows.

controlChecks.governs: Whether a mailbox can use the new Outlook for Windows at all (existing control, not specific to this feature)
